sources.inventory: All accessible public channels and enumerated direct-message conversations involving Contributor 01, from 2031-01-01 through the snapshot.
Enumerated project documents, comments, decision notes and meeting records accessible to the research account.
Enumerated issues, pull requests, reviews and release discussions in the relevant product repositories.

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Saturday's matinee had another cluster of duplicate-looking scans after the foyer access point restarted. The door team reverted to paper counts. Logging here before I forget.
records.title: Foyer restart report

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: I can take the offline reconciliation slice: define what the scanner stores, build the merge path, and give operations a way to see conflicts. I will need someone from device engineering for the retry behaviour.
records.title: Proposed ownership

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Goal: keep ticket validation usable during short connectivity gaps without admitting the same ticket twice. Pilot at two small venues in April. Contributor 01 owns reconciliation design and service implementation; Contributor 06 owns scanner firmware; Contributor 03 owns rollout and training.
records.title: Lantern Gate project brief

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Draft model: each scan receives a device event ID and local timestamp. The service accepts repeated uploads idempotently, but two different devices can still produce competing admits. Proposed first rule is earliest server-received event wins, with both events retained for audit.
records.title: Offline reconciliation notes

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: Server receipt order may reward whichever device reconnects first rather than the first door interaction. Can we use device time, assuming drift is bounded?
records.title: Comment on ordering

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Agreed that receipt order is not historical truth. Device clocks have shown multi-minute drift, so I suggest receipt order only as a deterministic admission rule, labelled as such. We should not display it as 'first scan'. I will add clock-offset telemetry for later analysis.
records.title: Ordering clarification

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Implement an idempotent upload endpoint keyed by venue, device and event ID. Preserve the raw payload and return the prior result on retry. Separate duplicate upload from cross-device ticket conflict.
records.title: Idempotent offline upload

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Adds the event ledger, idempotency key and replay-safe response. Includes migration and tests for repeated batches and interrupted requests. Conflict selection is deliberately not included.
records.title: Add replay-safe event ledger

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: The unique constraint and transaction boundary look right. Please add a test where the same event arrives in two overlapping batches.
records.title: Review request

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Added the overlapping-batch test and moved response reconstruction inside the transaction. Test fails without the constraint and passes with it.
records.title: Review update

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: Firmware can persist events, but storage is smaller than the brief assumes. At a busy door we have roughly three hours before old events rotate.
records.title: Device storage limit

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Three hours covers the stated short outages but makes silent overnight retention unsafe. I will cap service claims at two hours and add a backlog-age warning. Could you expose oldest queued event age?
records.title: Response to storage limit

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: Yes, but not in the first firmware build. I can expose queue depth now and age in the next sprint.
records.title: Telemetry sequencing

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Conflict screen draft: accepted, duplicate upload, competing device scan and unresolved. It must show that ordering is a system decision, not proof of which guest arrived first. Suggested action for a competing scan is supervisor verification, not automatic accusation.
records.title: Operator conflict states

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: Build conflict list and event detail using the service states from the operator note. Contributor 08 will implement the console; Contributor 01 will provide the API contract and sample payloads.
records.title: Conflict console

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Adds cross-device conflict classification, deterministic receipt-order selection, clock-offset capture and the console API. Sample payloads include ambiguous cases and avoid the phrase 'first scan'.
records.title: Classify competing scans

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: Blocking concern: events with an unknown ticket currently become conflicts, but they should remain invalid scans. Otherwise the pilot report will inflate conflict counts.
records.title: Invalid-ticket classification review

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Fixed by checking ticket validity before conflict grouping, and added the fixture you supplied. I also split invalid, repeated-upload and competing-admit metrics.
records.title: Classification correction

records.author: Contributor 09
records.body: The communal lunch fridge is being cleaned Thursday at 16:00. Anything unlabelled will be discarded.
records.title: Fridge cleaning

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Service ledger is in staging. Console shell is usable. Firmware uploads survive a restart, but queue-age telemetry is deferred. Training wording and a load rehearsal remain open.
records.title: Pilot readiness checkpoint

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Load rehearsal at 20 devices found the reconciliation worker falling behind because each event recalculates the full ticket history. I am changing it to incrementally update the current decision. Pilot-sized traffic is not safe on today's build.
records.title: Load rehearsal result

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Replaces full-history recalculation with a locked current-decision row. Rehearsal script improves from a 14-minute drain to under 90 seconds for the agreed pilot batch. Adds contention tests.
records.title: Incremental reconciliation worker

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: Approved for the pilot scale. This does not establish capacity for the largest venues; the script models 20 devices and one reconnect wave.
records.title: Scale-qualified approval

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Draft runbook covers outage entry, reconnect monitoring, conflict meanings, manual verification and rollback. The backlog-age field is marked unavailable in firmware build A; queue depth is the temporary signal.
records.title: Pilot operations runbook

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: I rewrote the door-team steps and added the escalation phone tree. Contributor 01's state definitions remain, but operations owns the procedure and delivery.
records.title: Operations edit

records.author: Contributor 02
records.body: Month-end expense exports are delayed while the tax-code mapping is corrected. This does not affect ticket settlement.
records.title: Expense export delay

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: Implements the conflict list, filters and detail panel. Uses Contributor 01's API and copy, with layout and accessibility changes from console review.
records.title: Conflict console implementation

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Go/no-go: service and console pass the pilot checklist. Device build still lacks oldest-event age, so outages beyond two hours require reverting to the existing manual procedure. April pilot remains on.
records.title: Pilot go decision

records.author: Contributor 03
records.container: Lantern Gate / Venue A pilot log
records.body: During a 17-minute network interruption, 1,842 scan events queued across 12 devices and later uploaded. Door validation continued. The ledger recorded 31 repeated uploads and six competing-device scans; staff manually checked all six. No confirmed double admission was reported in the shift log.
records.title: Venue A pilot log

records.author: Contributor 10
records.container: Lantern Gate / Venue A pilot log
records.body: One supervisor initially read 'accepted' as proof that the guest had arrived first. Training corrected this, and we should make the label more explicit before Venue B.
records.title: Label confusion

records.author: Contributor 01
records.container: Lantern Gate / Venue A pilot log
records.body: I will change the API display text to 'selected by system' and add the ordering explanation inline. This is a presentation fix; the stored decision and audit events do not change.
records.title: Label response

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Changes accepted-state display text to 'selected by system' and exposes a short receipt-order explanation for the console. No reconciliation logic change.
records.title: Clarify decision wording

records.author: Contributor 11
records.body: Venue B did not experience an outage, so it tells us little about offline recovery. Staff did use the conflict screen for two online cross-device scans and said the revised wording was clearer.
records.title: Venue B observation

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Recommendation: retain the feature at Venues A and B and expand to three similarly sized venues after queue-age telemetry ships. Evidence supports short interruptions at pilot scale, not estate-wide replacement of manual fallback. Service implementation was led by Contributor 01; firmware, console and operational rollout were separate owners.
records.title: Pilot review

records.author: Contributor 12
records.body: Next discussion is moving to Wednesday. The spare copies are in the blue cabinet.
records.title: Book club schedule

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: Adds oldest queued event age to heartbeat telemetry. Contributor 01 reviewed the field shape against the service contract; firmware implementation and device tests are mine.
records.title: Expose oldest queued event age

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Three additional small venues are now enabled. This is a controlled extension, not the large-hall rollout; support will review after four weeks.
records.title: Controlled extension

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Across the three added venues, two brief outages produced 2,406 queued events. Upload completed without operator intervention; four conflicts were manually checked and no confirmed double admissions were logged. One device showed a stale queue-age value after sleep, so support kept the two-hour fallback and opened a firmware defect. Larger-venue adoption remains undecided.
records.title: Four-week extension review

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: Queue-age heartbeat can remain stale after deep sleep until a new scan occurs. This affects warning accuracy, not retention or upload itself. Investigating wake-triggered refresh.
records.title: Stale queue-age telemetry

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: After the summer event, leadership approved a separate large-hall capacity trial. It has not started, and its results should not be folded into the spring follow-up.
records.title: Later capacity trial approval

attachments.body: Diagram showing queue-depth checks, service health and manual fallback branches.
